The implementation is complete and consistent. Here's what I changed and why.

## Changes made (source files only)

**1. Build configuration — `src/rt/CMakeLists.txt`**
Replaced the generic `-DUSE_MALLOC` with the allocator-specific `-DSNMALLOC_PASS_THROUGH`, kept as a `target_compile_definitions` compile definition on the `verona_rt` interface target (still gated on the `USE_ASAN` path, where pass-through is needed so ASAN can instrument allocations).

**2. Flag consumers — snmalloc headers** (`src/rt/external/snmalloc/src/mem/{alloc.h, globalalloc.h, threadalloc.h}`)
Renamed all 9 preprocessor guards (`#ifdef`/`#ifndef USE_MALLOC`) to `SNMALLOC_PASS_THROUGH` so the code that actually selects pass-through mode honors the new flag. Pure token swaps in `#ifdef`/`#ifndef` directives — semantically identical, just keyed on the new name — so the build config and the allocator agree end-to-end.

## What I deliberately did *not* touch

Per the CRITICAL constraint, I left all test files alone — the harness applies those patches:
- `src/rt/test/func/memory/memory.cc` — the `test_alloc_pool()` guard (`#ifndef USE_MALLOC` → `SNMALLOC_PASS_THROUGH`) that skips pool acquire/release under pass-through and otherwise checks that two acquires are distinct and a released-then-reacquired alloc returns the same object. It still shows `USE_MALLOC`; that's the patch's job.
- `src/rt/test/func/cown_weak_ref/cown_weak_ref.cc` — the `make_tree(10, …)` → `make_tree(9, …)` depth change.

I found no runtime source change implied for the weak-reference behavior — the existing scheduler/weak-ref logic already handles the tree; the depth-9 adjustment is purely a test parameter that the harness applies.

One note on scope: `src/rt/external/snmalloc` is a **git submodule**, so the header renames live in the submodule's working tree rather than the parent repo's tracked diff (upstream, this rename shipped via a submodule bump). The parent-repo deliverable is the `CMakeLists.txt` change. I still applied the header renames so the flag is honored coherently in this working tree. Either way, the default (non-ASAN) build leaves neither flag defined, so the pool tests exercise the real allocator as expected.
